extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (prospective ERC Starting Grant applicants), their prospective Host Institutions and support staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing and submitting an ERC Starting Grant proposal, covering applicant eligibility, host institution requirements, application components, funding rules and the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since completion of PhD (Extensions are possible under certain circumstances — see the latest ERC Work Programme), a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2-7 year window can be extended in defined circumstances per the ERC Work Programme. Applicants should demonstrate both past supervised achievements and potential to lead independent research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research field eligibility (bottom-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yearly calls cover all scientific fields; applicants are not required to fit pre-specified topic lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution and submission entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted by a single Principal Investigator (PI) in conjunction with and on behalf of their Host Institution, called the applicant legal entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any type of legal entity (universities, research centres, undertakings) can host the PI, but the host legal entity must be based in an EU Member State or an Associated Country. The PI does not need to be employed at the host at submission time, but a mutual agreement and the host’s commitment are necessary should the proposal succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution commitment to PI independence and project management
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded to the Host Institution with the explicit commitment that this institution offers appropriate conditions for the Principal Investigator independently to direct the research and manage its funding for the duration of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions must demonstrate and commit to providing the environment, resources and managerial autonomy required for the PI to run the project independently throughout the grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (known as a Host Institution/HI) located in one of the EU Member States or Associated Countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host may be the applicant’s current employer or another eligible HI; see programme pages for details on specific country/entity eligibility (e.g., guidance on UK legal entities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancies for team members can be published on Euraxess-Jobs. Initiatives ('Implementing Arrangements') exist to host non-European scientists in ERC-funded teams; check agreements and mobility provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants may be awarded up to €1.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration). An additional €0.5 million can be made available to cover eligible 'start-up' costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU or an associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. The completed proposal should be submitted by the specified closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on the ERC page, the Participant Portal and in the Official Journal. Ensure all administrative, proposal and annex documents are included before submission; incomplete submissions risk being declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and deadline rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals. The completed proposal should be submitted by the specified closing date. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by simply submitting a new version, which will overwrite the old one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with the Participant Portal submission service and related online manuals. Submit early where possible because deadlines are final; each submission receives an acknowledgement of receipt by e-mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — excellence as the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who evaluate proposals on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It will be applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellence covers both the quality and ambition of the research and the PI's capacity to carry it out. Only proposals meeting excellence standards (as assessed by reviewers) progress in ranking and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process — peer reviewers, quality threshold and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are in charge of assessing and scoring the proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External experts evaluate eligible proposals; passing the quality threshold is necessary but not sufficient — final funding depends on ranking and available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation structure — panels and remote referees
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 25 panels, each covering a sub-section of one of three domains (SH, LS, PE). Each ERC panel consists of a chairman and 10-16 members selected on the basis of their scientific reputation. Evaluations also rely on input from remote experts external to the panel, called referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chairs are published before the deadline. Panel Members are published after the evaluation process is concluded. Referees bring specialised expertise beyond the panel generalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility checking and feedback timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: After the deadline: The ERC will check whether your proposal meets the call’s eligibility criteria. External experts will evaluate all the eligible proposals. You will receive further information as your proposal progresses through the evaluation. See 'Ongoing evaluations' for the feedback timetables for calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for the eligibility check and peer review; consult the call-specific timetable for expected feedback dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-call preparation and application writing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: find which ERC grant and call is suitable; identify the host institution and team members; contact the National Contact Point (NCP). Once the call is open: read the call documents carefully; contact the host institution and gather all details; start writing your proposal and allow time for others to review your draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use support from NCPs, peers and other scientists for feedback; familiarise yourself with online submission guides and manuals; allow time for institutional agreement processes and internal reviews before final submission.
